categories.main_business_segments: Tigerair Taiwan operates primarily as a low-cost airline providing international passenger air transport services. Its business includes scheduled and non-scheduled international charter flights, cargo transport, and ground agency services such as airport operations and cargo handling. The company also offers ancillary services including in-flight meals, duty-free shopping, and travel-related products through an integrated e-commerce platform.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company utilizes advanced aviation technologies including a fleet of Airbus A320 and A320neo aircraft, with plans to fully transition to 15 new-generation A320neo aircraft by 2028 to improve fuel efficiency and reduce emissions. It employs digital platforms such as a Customer Data Platform (CDP), Customer Relationship Management (CRM) systems enhanced by AI for precision marketing, and integrated aircraft operation systems for crew scheduling and maintenance. Tigerair Taiwan also implements ISO 27001 and ISO 27017 certified information security management systems.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Tigerair Taiwan serves primarily individual travelers, especially young adults aged 20-39, focusing on international routes to Japan, South Korea, Thailand, Macau, Vietnam, and other Asian destinations. The Japanese market is the largest revenue source, with 20 destinations served. The airline targets both domestic Taiwanese travelers and foreign tourists, including a growing number of Japanese visitors to Taiwan.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates mainly in the Asia-Pacific region, with key markets including Taiwan, Japan, South Korea, Thailand, Macau, and Vietnam. It serves 29 destinations and 40 routes as of 2025, with offices and branches in Taiwan, Japan, the Philippines, Thailand, and China (Zhangjiajie).
categories.supply_chain_position: Tigerair Taiwan operates primarily in the midstream segment of the aviation supply chain as an airline carrier. It relies on upstream suppliers such as aircraft manufacturers, leasing companies, and fuel providers, and serves downstream customers including the general public, travel agencies, and freight forwarding industries.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The company focuses on fleet modernization with the introduction of fuel-efficient A320neo aircraft, digital transformation including AI-driven personalized marketing and integrated ticketing platforms, and enhancing passenger experience through innovative in-flight services and ancillary products. It emphasizes sustainable development with ESG initiatives, including carbon emission reduction, energy efficiency, and corporate governance improvements. Planned R&D projects include upgrading flight and hotel booking systems, crew scheduling, and financial systems.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is primarily generated through passenger ticket sales, which constitute over 96% of total revenue. Additional income streams include ancillary services such as in-flight meals, baggage fees, duty-free sales, and travel-related product sales via an integrated e-commerce platform. The company also earns revenue from cargo transport and ground handling services.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Tigerair Taiwan is positioned as the only Taiwanese low-cost carrier and holds a 9% market share in Taiwan's international and cross-strait air transport market. Major competitors include EVA Air (41.5% market share), China Airlines (35.3%), and STARLUX Airlines (12.7%). Tigerair Taiwan is the third-largest airline serving Japanese destinations from Taiwan, following Japan Airlines and All Nippon Airways.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In 2024, Tigerair Taiwan reported operating revenues of NT$16.42 billion, a 31.7% increase from 2023, and a net profit after tax of NT$2.77 billion, a 51.7% increase year-over-year. The company operated approximately 18,700 international flights carrying 2.9 million passengers. Total assets increased by 24% to NT$22.38 billion, and total equity grew by 80.35% to NT$7.63 billion. The company has shown strong profitability and growth, with plans for continued expansion and fleet renewal.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Tigerair Taiwan differentiates itself as Taiwan's only low-cost airline offering extensive route options including secondary and tertiary cities, catering to young and spontaneous travelers. It emphasizes personalized travel experiences through AI-driven marketing and a comprehensive ancillary product portfolio. The airline focuses on operational safety, sustainability with a modern fuel-efficient fleet, and enhanced passenger services such as gourmet in-flight meals featuring local Taiwanese flavors and partnerships with renowned brands. Its flexible and adaptive business model supports competitive pricing and diverse travel options.
